subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Berners-Lee Gives Away the Web
description: A fast breakdown of Berners-Lee Gives Away the Web for builders.

hook.text: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989. He could have patented it. He gave it away for free.

buildup.text: His employer CERN supported the decision. A free, open web would connect researchers.

discovery.text: Because the web was free, anyone could build on it. That openness created the entire modern internet economy.

twist.text: Berners-Lee is not a billionaire. If he had charged even a tiny royalty, he would be the richest person in history.

climax.text: Berners-Lee chose impact over profit. Some decisions are measured in what they enable, not what they earn.

punchline.text: Free the invention, change the world. Impact over profit, forever.

quiz.question: Why did Berners-Lee give the web away for free?
options: He didn't think it was valuable
A free web would spread and connect people in ways a proprietary one never could
